title: Nakhoda Masjid | Kolkata Trips
description: Discover Nakhoda Masjid Kolkata with its history, architecture, prayer timings, entry details, nearby attractions, visitor tips, and how to reach.
textContent: Nakhoda Masjid Standing proudly in the heart of Kolkata’s bustling Burrabazar, Nakhoda Masjid is the largest mosque in Kolkata and one of the city’s most recognizable religious landmarks. Its magnificent red sandstone façade, soaring minarets, and massive central dome dominate the skyline, attracting worshippers, photographers, architecture enthusiasts, and tourists alike. Built in the early 20th century, Nakhoda Masjid represents not only Islamic architecture at its finest but also Kolkata’s multicultural heritage. Every Friday and during major Islamic festivals, thousands of devotees gather here for prayers, making it one of the most vibrant places of worship in eastern India. Whether you are exploring Kolkata’s heritage or seeking remarkable architectural landmarks, Nakhoda Masjid deserves a place on your itinerary. History of Nakhoda Masjid The history of Nakhoda Masjid dates back to 1926, when construction began under the patronage of Abdar Rahim Osman, a wealthy Kutchi Memon businessman originally from Gujarat. The word “Nakhoda” means “Captain” or “Mariner”, reflecting the maritime heritage of the Kutchi Memon community, many of whom were successful traders and sailors. Inspired by the grandeur of the Mughal architectural tradition, the mosque was designed using red sandstone sourced from Rajasthan. It took several years to complete and soon became the principal mosque of Kolkata. Today, Nakhoda Masjid serves as the spiritual headquarters for the Kutchi Memon community while welcoming Muslims and visitors from across India and the world. Architecture and Design of Nakhoda Masjid Nakhoda Masjid is one of the finest examples of Indo-Islamic architecture in eastern India. Massive Central Dome The mosque features a spectacular central dome rising prominently above the prayer hall, inspired by Mughal architectural traditions. Twin Minarets Two elegant minarets, each rising approximately 46 metres (151 feet), frame the entrance and can be seen from various parts of central Kolkata. Red Sandstone Construction The extensive use of red sandstone gives the mosque its distinctive appearance and recalls the architecture of Mughal monuments such as the Jama Masjid in Delhi. Spacious Prayer Hall The expansive prayer hall is designed to accommodate thousands of worshippers during daily and Friday prayers. Beautiful Arches and Calligraphy Intricate Islamic calligraphy, marble detailing, decorative arches, and symmetrical layouts enhance the mosque’s spiritual atmosphere. Religious Importance Nakhoda Masjid is the principal mosque of Kolkata and plays an important role during: Daily congregational prayers Friday (Jumu’ah) prayers Ramadan Eid-ul-Fitr Eid-ul-Adha Islamic lectures and religious gatherings During Ramadan, the mosque becomes especially lively as thousands gather for evening prayers and community meals. Timings The mosque remains open throughout the day, with access centered around the five daily prayers. General Visiting Hours Approximately 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM Visitors should avoid entering during prayer times unless they are participating in prayers. Prayer timings vary daily according to the Islamic calendar. Entry Fee Entry Fee: Free Photography from the exterior is generally permitted. Interior photography should only be done after obtaining permission from mosque authorities. Best Time to Visit The ideal time to visit Nakhoda Masjid is: October to March for pleasant weather Early morning for peaceful surroundings Late afternoon for beautiful lighting During Ramadan (with respect for worshippers) to experience the vibrant spiritual atmosphere Visitors should avoid peak Friday prayer hours if they wish to explore the mosque comfortably. How to Reach Nakhoda Masjid By Metro The nearest metro stations include: Mahatma Gandhi Road Central Esplanade (slightly farther) From the station, the mosque is easily accessible by taxi, auto-rickshaw, or on foot. By Road Located in Burrabazar, the mosque is well connected by: Taxi App-based cabs Private vehicles Public buses Traffic can be heavy during business hours. By Railway The mosque is within easy reach of: Howrah Railway Station Sealdah Railway Station Both stations are about 15–20 minutes away, depending on traffic. Nearby Attractions Combine your visit with several nearby attractions: Burrabazar – One of Asia’s largest wholesale markets. Marble Palace – A magnificent 19th-century mansion with art collections. Howrah Bridge – Kolkata’s iconic engineering landmark. Magen David Synagogue – One of India’s most impressive synagogues. College Street – The world’s largest second-hand book market. These sites can easily be included in a Full Day Kolkata City Tour. Visitor Tips and Guidelines Dress modestly, covering shoulders and knees. Remove footwear before entering the prayer area. Maintain silence inside the mosque. Avoid visiting during Friday prayers if sightseeing. Seek permission before photographing interiors. Respect worshippers and religious customs. Women should carry a scarf to cover their heads while inside the prayer hall. Keep mobile phones on silent mode. Interesting Facts About Nakhoda Masjid It is the largest mosque in Kolkata. The mosque can accommodate around 10,000 worshippers at a time. Its design was inspired by Delhi’s famous Jama Masjid. The mosque was commissioned by the Kutchi Memon community. The name “Nakhoda” means “Captain” or “Mariner.” The mosque remains one of Kolkata’s most significant Islamic landmarks. Why Visit Nakhoda Masjid? Nakhoda Masjid offers much more than a place of worship. It is a remarkable blend of spirituality, history, architecture, and community life. Its towering minarets, magnificent prayer hall, and rich cultural heritage make it one of Kolkata’s most memorable landmarks. Whether you are interested in architecture, photography, religion, or the city’s diverse heritage, a visit to Nakhoda Masjid provides an enriching glimpse into Kolkata’s multicultural identity. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Why is Nakhoda Masjid famous? It is famous for being the largest mosque in Kolkata, its impressive Mughal-inspired architecture, and its importance as a major center of Islamic worship in eastern India. 2. Where is Nakhoda Masjid located? Nakhoda Masjid is located in the Burrabazar area of central Kolkata, West Bengal. 3. Is there an entry fee for Nakhoda Masjid? No. Entry is free for all visitors. 4. What are the visiting hours? Visitors can generally visit between 6:00 AM and 8:00 PM, though access may be restricted during prayer times. 5. Can tourists enter the mosque? Yes. Visitors of all faiths are welcome, provided they dress modestly and respect the mosque’s rules and ongoing prayers. 6. Who built Nakhoda Masjid? The mosque was commissioned by Abdar Rahim Osman of the Kutchi Memon community. 7. What does “Nakhoda” mean? “Nakhoda” means “Captain” or “Mariner,” reflecting the seafaring heritage of the Kutchi Memon community. 8. How many people can the mosque accommodate? The mosque can accommodate approximately 10,000 worshippers at a time. 9. Is photography allowed? Photography of the exterior is generally allowed. Permission should be sought before taking photographs inside the mosque. 10. Which metro station is nearest? Mahatma Gandhi Road Metro Station is among the nearest stations to Nakhoda Masjid. 11. What is the best time to visit? October to March offers the most comfortable weather. Early mornings and late afternoons are ideal for sightseeing. 12. Which attractions can be visited nearby? Nearby attractions include Marble Palace, Howrah Bridge, Burrabazar, Magen David Synagogue, and College Street. 13. Is Nakhoda Masjid included in Kolkata sightseeing tours? Yes. It is often included in heritage and customized Kolkata city tours, particularly those focusing on religious landmarks and Old Kolkata.
